about: Web Summit's editions in Lisbon, 2016 to 2025, with the attendance figure where a public source other than websummit.com gives one. On 11 November 2026 whatever rested only on websummit.com was taken off (its licence does not let us republish data from its site); each figure here has another public source, cited; each comes back when one is found. Status says how far we read: read (a public page read), tertiary (Wikipedia's table), none (no figure we may show).

ui.empty: Tap an edition to see its dates, the figure and where it comes from.
ui.caption: Attendance at Web Summit in Lisbon, as public sources report it. Solid: read in a public source (a news agency's headline for 2024; Portugal's trade agency for 2025). Paler: from Wikipedia's table (2016 to 2018, and about 70,000 for 2022). Marked n/a: no figure we may show. Web Summit's own releases are not used: its licence does not let us republish data from its site, so on 11 November 2026 we took off whatever rested only on it.
ui.cautions: 2025's 71,386 is below 2024's 71,528, so 'record attendance' does not hold for 2025 in these sources; the record claimed for 2025 is for investors (1,857, up 74%). One recap gives 71,368.

No figure here. The organiser's own figure rested only on websummit.com and was taken off on 11 November 2026 (licence); a city release that carries it could not be read by a machine (it refuses automated readers), so it is not used. It comes back when another public source we may read carries it.

Lusa, the Portuguese news agency, headlined 'Web Summit has record-breaking 71,528 participants' on 12 November 2024 (midweek; the body is for subscribers and was not read). The organiser's own breakdown (countries, investors, speakers, media, delegations) rested only on websummit.com and was taken off on 11 November 2026 (licence).

Portugal's trade agency AICEP (portugalglobal.pt, a Lusa report of 12 November 2025, midweek) says the organiser reported 71,386 participants from 157 countries; 1,857 investors from 86 countries, up 74% from 1,066 the year before; and 2,725 startups from 108 countries, 40% with women among the founders. The organiser's longer breakdown rested only on websummit.com and was taken off on 11 November 2026 (licence). 71,386 is below Lusa's 71,528 for 2024, so 'record attendance' does not hold for 2025; the record the organiser claims is for investors. One recap gives 71,368.
